1	# Agent Note: Content-addressed identity and the composition manifest event
2	
3	Status: proposed
4	
5	English | [中文](2026-09-05-composition-manifest.zh.md)
6	
7	## Problem
8	
9	Every identity in the harness names a slot rather than the bytes in it. A `ComponentId` is "derived from its kind and the owning seam's stable name, never from mount order" ([`dsh-components`](../../../../packages/components/components/README.md)), a skill is addressed by its kebab-case name, a prompt section and a tool by their registered names, a preset by its directory name, and a plugin by its package name. Editing a skill body in place leaves all of those addresses unchanged, so a leaderboard cannot separate the generation before the edit from the generation after it, a rollback has no earlier address to return to, and a decontamination check has nothing to key on — the failure the [four-goal-workflows note](2026-09-05-four-goal-workflows.md) records under its rejected "single mutable knowledge store" alternative and forbids in principle P5.
10	
11	Nothing durable records which components a session had in play. The `request/header` event carries each epoch's assembled system prompt text and tool schemas, which is enough to replay a request and not enough to name what produced it: it carries no component identity, provenance, lineage, or registry layer; a skill body loaded through the `skill` tool reaches the transcript as a tool result and never the header; and a dynamic package mounted through [`tool-cordis`](../../../../packages/extensions/tool-cordis/README.md) that registers no tool is invisible in it. The component registry itself is composition-time state that dies with the process, as [the component-registry seam note](2026-09-01-component-registry-seam.md) states outright.
12	
13	Four consumers are blocked on that gap. [`dsh-scorekeeper`](../../../../packages/improvement/scorekeeper/README.md) ships no `composition_hash`, `component_ids`, or `skills_used` field because no event supplies one. W4 stage 1's invariant — a skill result whose digest is absent from the manifest fails — has no manifest to check against. The trajectory exporter can withhold a held-out environment but cannot tell a curated composition from one an agent mutated mid-session, so a synthesized skill body can reach a training set unannounced. And W4 stage 9's knowledge ledger has no address to mirror its entries against, which is what makes "a ledger entry with no matching manifest occurrence never counts as having been in play" enforceable rather than aspirational.
14	
15	## Proposal
16	
17	**One digest function, one address form.** [`dsh-components`](../../../../packages/components/components/README.md) gains `ComponentDigest` (a `Branded<'ComponentDigest'>` from `dsh-brand`) and two pure functions: `componentDigest(kind, canonical)` returns the lowercase SHA-256 hex of `` `${kind}\n${JSON.stringify(canonical)}` ``, and `componentAddress(id, digest)` returns `` `${id}@${digest}` ``. The kind is inside the hashed bytes so two kinds whose canonical values coincide never share an address. The digest is the full 64 hex characters everywhere it is stored or compared, matching `environmentContentHashes` in [`dsh-environments`](../../../../packages/improvement/environments/README.md); truncating it for a card or a table is a presentation choice that never enters a log or the ledger. `ComponentDescriptor` gains a required `digest: ComponentDigest` and a required `digestBasis: 'content' | 'registration'`. As landed, `canonical` is typed `ComponentCanonical` — a JSON value — so a producer cannot hand the hash a value `JSON.stringify` would drop, and `componentAddress` returns a plain string: an address is minted and compared, never received across a boundary that a brand would guard.
18	
19	**Each producer owns its canonical value.** The registry ships no per-kind canonicalization for the same reason it ships no kind: each producer declares its `ComponentKindMap` member by declaration merging and exports the pure function that canonicalizes it, so a kind added later needs no change in the registry or in the manifest writer. The table below fixes the canonical value of every kind this note introduces. As landed, the exported function is the kind's digest rather than its bare canonical value — `agentProviderDigest(provider)`, and `skillDigest(definition)` as the skill row already names — so a consumer recomputing an address calls the producer instead of rebuilding the canonical value from the table.
20	
21	**The registry becomes layered.** `ComponentRegistry` was one flat `Map`, so it could not answer "what does this agent see". It uses `ScopedLayers` from `dsh-scope`, exactly as [`ctx.tools`](../../../../packages/core/tools/README.md) and [`ctx.skills`](../../../../packages/skill/skill/README.md) already do: `register()` files into the calling context's scope, and `list({ kind, scope })` merges the global layer with the viewing scope's chain, the nearest layer's entry winning a duplicate id. A descriptor read back through a scope carries `layer: 'global' | 'agent'` — `global` when the winning registration sits in the global layer, `agent` when it sits in a layer of that agent's scope chain. A deeper chain still reads as `agent`, because a subagent writes its own manifest into its own session. Ids are unique per layer, so a duplicate in one layer still throws `COMPONENT_DUPLICATE_ID` while the same id in a different layer shadows.
22	
23	The derived `layer` rides `ComponentView`, a distinct read type extending `ComponentDescriptor`, rather than an optional descriptor field: a producer registers a descriptor and cannot assert its own layer, and a reader always has one. `get(id, { scope })` takes the same viewing scope as `list({ kind, scope })`, the `SkillViewOptions` pattern `dsh-skill` already uses for its two reads. The registry publishes no change notification — the rejected `components/change` alternative below is why — so the `ScopedLayers` change callback is an explained no-op.
24	
25	**The manifest writer reads one registry.** `@deepseek-ai/dsh-components-manifest` at `packages/components/components-manifest/` injects `agents` and `components` and nothing else. On `agent/pre-step` it calls `next()` first, recomputes `ctx.components.list({ scope: agent })` for the calling agent, compares the resulting `compositionSha256` with the last `composition/manifest` event in that session's log, and appends a new event through `agent.session.append()` only when the two differ — the shape [`dsh-budget-policy`](../../../../packages/guard/budget-policy/README.md) already uses to fold and append before a step opens. Recomputing rather than tracking incrementally is what keeps it correct across HMR disposal, a preset mounted after creation, and scope shadowing: the writer holds no subscription state that any of those three orderings could invalidate.
26	
27	**Every other seam reaches the manifest through an adapter.** The one-adapter-per-seam rule [the component-registry note](2026-09-01-component-registry-seam.md) established is what keeps the writer from reading registries it does not own, and each adapter follows its seam's own change notification: `dsh-components-tools` follows `tools/change`, `dsh-components-prompt` follows `system-prompt/change`, `dsh-components-skills` follows `tools/result` for the `skill` tool, `dsh-components-presets` follows the `agent-preset/selected` Cordis event, and the shipped `dsh-components-subagents` already follows `subagent/provider-added` and `subagent/provider-removed`. One seam emits nothing today: the dynamic Cordis runner behind `tool-cordis` reports no change when a package is defined, run, stopped, or removed, so `dsh-cordis-host-runner` gains an unfiltered `cordis/dynamic-changed(agent, pluginId)` Cordis event — `@mode emit`, not scope-filtered, so no scope-scan metadata applies — and `dsh-components-packages` follows it.
28	
29	**A skill is in play once its body is loaded, not once it is listed.** `ctx.skills.list()` returns summaries without bodies, so registering every discoverable skill would need a body load per catalog entry per step and would still address a summary rather than the knowledge. `dsh-skill` therefore exports `skillDigest(definition)` over the loaded definition, the `skill` tool's canonical output value gains a `digest` field (absent from `renderSkillContent`, so the model-facing text is unchanged, and durable in `tool/result`), and `SkillInvocationSource` gains the same field so the user-explicit `/name` injection records it too. `dsh-components-skills` registers a `skill` component from either durable record through `exec.agent.ctx`, never by re-parsing the rendered `<skill_content>` block. Skills that were reachable but never loaded stay out of the manifest; the catalog they came from is already durable as the `skill-catalog` message source.
30	
31	## What each kind hashes
32	
33	| Kind | Canonical value | Basis | Producer |
34	|---|---|---|---|
35	| `skill` | `[name, description, whenToUse ?? null, invocation.modelInvocable, invocation.userInvocable, metadata ?? null, content]` from the loaded `SkillDefinition` | content | `dsh-components-skills`, over `skillDigest()` in `dsh-skill` |
36	| `prompt-section` | `[name, order, complete === true, text]` when `PromptSection.text` is a string; `[name, order, complete === true, null]` when it is a provider evaluated per assembly | content, else registration | `dsh-components-prompt` |
37	| `tool` | the model-facing `ToolSchema` as `ctx.tools.schemas(agent)` projects it: name, description, parameter schema, output schema, in the registry's own field order | content | `dsh-components-tools` |
38	| `preset` | `[id, trust, rows]`, where `rows` is the preset's composition after `include` resolution as `[id, name, config, disabled]` per row, with every `name` that resolves to a path rewritten relative to the preset directory | content | `dsh-components-presets` |
39	| `plugin` | `[packageName, version, patchLayerSha256]`, the version from the resolved package manifest and `patchLayerSha256` the SHA-256 over the ordered `cordis.patch.yml` rows of the bundles in force | content | `dsh-components-packages`, over `ctx.loader.entries()` |
40	| `dynamic-package` | `[pluginId, packageId, hostSource, clientSource]` from `ctx.dynamicCordisRunner.inspectPlugin(agent, pluginId)` | content | `dsh-components-packages` |
41	| `agent-provider` | `[provider]` | registration | `dsh-components-subagents` |
42	
43	A digest never covers the viewing scope, the working directory, a wall-clock time, an absolute path (`SkillDefinition.path`, `SkillResourceBase`'s directory, `AgentPreset.path`), a discovery `source` or `rank`, a provider name, or any value a registry computes per assembly. Two hosts that discovered the same skill under different roots, and the same body re-registered through a different provider, therefore address identically; one byte changed in a skill body, a tool parameter description, a static prompt section, or a preset row moves the digest. A `registration`-basis digest addresses the registration and not the bytes the model saw, which is the honest statement for a section whose text is a function of the assembly; the rendered bytes stay where they already are, in `request/header`.
44	
45	## The `composition/manifest` event
46	
47	`dsh-components-manifest` declaration-merges one member into `SessionEventMap` in `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session/types`. It is **log-only** and carries no `@mode` tag: a session log event has no dispatch mode, it rides the single `session/event` emit, and `gen-persistence-catalog` rejects the tag outright — the repo's `@mode` and payload-`@param` rules govern the Cordis bus event this note adds, not this one. It is **required-on-read**, without the envelope's `ignorable: true` marker, because every consumer below keys a refusal on it: a build that cannot interpret the type would otherwise fold a scoreboard row and write an export line for a session it cannot prove was unquarantined ([the version mechanism](../../implemented/architecture/2026-08-10-session-log-version-mechanism.md)). Its payload fields, each carrying its own JSDoc so [the generated catalog](../../../../docs/persistence-catalog.md) documents them:
48	
49	- `kind: 'composition/manifest'` and `version: 1`, the self-declared payload version the environment stamp also carries.
50	- `reason`: why this manifest was written — `'session-start'`, `'preset-mounted'`, `'skill-loaded'`, `'tools-changed'`, `'prompt-changed'`, or `'package-mounted'`, decided by which kinds changed since the previous manifest.
51	- `presetId`: the preset the agent runs, resolved through `resolveSessionPreset()`; absent when the deployment composes none.
52	- `components`: one entry per component in play, ordered by `id`, each `{ id, digest, kind, provenance, lineage?, layer, digestBasis }`.
53	- `compositionSha256`: SHA-256 over the ordered `id@digest` addresses joined by newlines — the deduplication key and the `composition_hash` the scoreboard row wants.
54	- `dynamicPackagesMounted`: whether any entry has kind `dynamic-package`.
55	- `synthesized`: the ids of every entry whose `provenance` is `synthesized`, in the same order.
56	
57	The four-goal note's sketch lists a `seq` field; the envelope already carries `seq`, so the payload does not repeat it. The first manifest is appended before the session's first `request/header`, because `agent/pre-step` runs before the step assembles its request and the preset has already settled by then — a preset chosen after creation commits `agent-preset/selected` while the session is still blank. Every later change to the set in play produces the next differing manifest at the next step, which is the first step whose model request that change can reach.
58	
59	## Quarantine
60	
61	A session is quarantined when its latest manifest reports `dynamicPackagesMounted` or a non-empty `synthesized`, and equally when its log carries no manifest at all: a session that cannot prove what was in play is exactly as unusable as one that mounted code an agent wrote. `SessionFacts.identity` in [`dsh-scorekeeper`](../../../../packages/improvement/scorekeeper/README.md) gains a `composition` group folded from the latest manifest — `compositionSha256`, the entry count, `presetId`, `dynamicPackagesMounted`, and `synthesized` — plus `skillsUsed`, the `id@digest` addresses of every `skill` entry any manifest of the session named. Its `./invariant` companion gains one relation beside the three it checks today: for every `tool/result` of the `skill` tool carrying a digest, some `composition/manifest` at or before that event's `seq` names a `skill` component with that digest, and a result whose digest appears in no manifest is reported as a record disagreeing with its own log. [`dsh-trajectories`](../../../../packages/improvement/trajectories/README.md) gains `includeQuarantined?: boolean` on `TrajectoryExportRequest` and a `quarantined` count on `TrajectoryExportReport`, symmetric with `includeHeldOut` and `heldOut`: absent, the export refuses every quarantined session and accounts for it in the count rather than dropping it silently. The complementary quarantine — a Harness Engineer proposal that touches an evaluator-owned path — belongs to W1 stage 7 and stays there.
62	
63	## The knowledge ledger
64	
65	`@deepseek-ai/dsh-archive` at `packages/improvement/archive/` (`ctx.archive`) holds the cross-session records over [`ctx.storage.domain`](../../../../packages/storage/storage-domain/README.md), through a `defineDomain` spec whose record schemas are zod, routed to whichever backend the deployment configures. Two tables: `variants`, keyed by the `HarnessVariant` id (base commit plus patch-set hash) with the fields the four-goal note fixes — `parent`, `operator`, `patch`, `scores`, `evaluations[]`, `children[]`, `status`, `proposer`; and `generations`, keyed by `id@digest` with `componentId`, `digest`, `kind`, `provenance`, `lineage` (the parent's address, absent for a root), `evidenceSessions[]`, `results`, and `status`. A mutation mints a new row rather than rewriting one, so a generation's bytes and its address never diverge.
66	
67	`status` is `alive`, `dominated`, `promoted`, or `deprecated`. `alive` is evaluated or newly minted and still eligible for parent sampling; `dominated` lost to another generation of its lineage on every measured cell and stays sampleable and auditable, never deleted, which is the archive semantics the four-goal note's rejected best-only alternative exists to preserve; `promoted` carries the `PromotionDecision` that moved it into curated source; `deprecated` is what the department scoreboard writes once a paired present-versus-absent delta has stayed at or below zero over the configured number of runs. Lineage is stored on both ends — `lineage` on the child for the auditor walking up, `children[]` on the parent for the sampler's `1/(1+children)` weight — and a status change appends a revision rather than removing a row.
68	
69	The ledger's `./invariant` companion owns the manifest-versus-ledger relation, an assertion over mutable data against the authoritative event stream the [package invariant rules](../../../../packages/AGENTS.md) require: for every generation row, each session named in `evidenceSessions` must carry a `composition/manifest` whose `components` hold that exact `id@digest`. A row that names an evidence session with no matching occurrence is reported and never counts as having been in play, so a promotion cannot rest on a session the component was not actually composed into.
70	
71	## Alternatives considered
72	
73	**Derive the manifest from `request/header`.** The header already records the assembled system prompt and every tool schema of each epoch, so a fold over it would need no new event. It is rejected because the header carries rendered text and no identity: provenance, lineage, and layer are absent, a loaded skill body never reaches it, and a dynamic package that registers no tool leaves it unchanged — precisely the three cases the quarantine has to catch.
74	
75	**Keep the registry composition-time only, with no session event.** `ctx.components` is already the inventory, so a consumer could read it live. It is rejected because every consumer here reads persisted logs after the fact — the scorekeeper folds them, the exporter writes from them, the ledger invariant checks against them — and composition-time truth dies with the process.
76	
77	**One manifest per session, written at creation.** A single record would be smaller and simpler to fold. It is rejected because a skill load, a preset switch, and a dynamic mount all change the set mid-session, and a start-of-session record would report a clean composition for exactly the sessions the quarantine exists to flag.
78	
79	**Hash each component's rendered contribution.** Hashing what the model actually received would tie the digest to the bytes in the transcript. It is rejected because rendering depends on the working directory, the wall clock, and the viewing scope, so two identical compositions on two hosts would address differently and decontamination would key on noise; `request/header` already owns the rendered bytes, and the manifest owns identity.
80	
81	**Put the per-kind canonicalization in the manifest writer.** One switch over kinds inside the writer would avoid an adapter per seam. It is rejected because the writer would then have to know every kind, which is the coupling `ComponentKindMap`'s declaration merging removes, and a kind added downstream could not be digested at all.
82	
83	**A monotonic version counter per component instead of a content address.** A `skill@3` label is shorter and human-readable. It is rejected for the reason the four-goal note's "single mutable knowledge store" alternative was: a counter is authored rather than derived, so two hosts that refine the same body disagree on the number, a body restored from an ancestor gets a new number instead of its old address, and no consumer can verify the label against the bytes.
84	
85	**A `components/change` event with an incremental writer.** Mirroring `tools/change` would let the writer maintain the manifest between steps instead of recomputing it. It is rejected because recomputation is one registry read and one hash per step and cannot be wrong, while an incremental writer would have to stay correct across HMR disposal, preset remounts, and scope shadowing; no consumer in this note needs a change notification, so the event is not added until one does.
86	
87	**The ledger as session events rather than storage.** Recording generations in the log would keep everything on one plane. It is rejected because a ledger spans sessions and outlives every one of them, and because the manifest-versus-ledger invariant needs two planes to be a real check: an entry that is itself a session event could not be contradicted by the session events it cites.
88	
89	## Acceptance criteria
90	
91	- A Loader-booted composition at `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/composition-manifest/` appends one `composition/manifest` before the session's first `request/header`; the event names the preset id, carries one entry per component in play with a `digest`, `provenance`, `layer`, and `digestBasis`, and its `compositionSha256` equals a recomputation from the ordered `id@digest` addresses in the persisted log.
92	- In the same fixture, the agent calls the `skill` tool once; a second manifest follows with `reason: 'skill-loaded'`, one added `skill` entry whose digest equals `skillDigest()` over that body, and a different `compositionSha256`. A step that changes nothing appends no third event.
93	- Two runs of that fixture under different temporary workspace roots and different `DSH_HOME` values produce byte-identical `compositionSha256` values, proving absolute paths, discovery roots, and timestamps are outside every digest.
94	- `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/composition-manifest-mutation/` runs the same composition twice with one byte of the skill body changed between the runs; exactly one entry's digest differs, `compositionSha256` differs, and every other entry is unchanged.
95	- `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/composition-manifest-quarantine/` composes `tool-cordis`, defines and runs a dynamic package, and proves the next manifest reports `dynamicPackagesMounted: true` with the package's id in `synthesized`; the trajectory export then withholds that session and counts it as `quarantined`, and the same export with `includeQuarantined` writes it.
96	- A keyless unit test over a synthetic log proves the scorekeeper invariant reports a `skill` tool result whose digest appears in no preceding manifest, and accepts the same result once a manifest names it; a second proves a session with no manifest at all folds to a quarantined record rather than a clean one.
97	- A keyless unit test in `packages/improvement/archive/tests/` proves the ledger invariant reports a generation row whose evidence session carries no manifest occurrence of its `id@digest`, and accepts the row once one exists.
98	- The persisted-log snapshot suite `examples/headless-agent` owns records the manifest events for the scenario that composes the manifest writer; the event is log-only and changes no model-visible text, so the required coverage is the persisted log rather than a transcript re-record ([testing policy](../../../../docs/testing.md)).
99	
100	## Rollout
101	
102	1. **Landed.** `dsh-components`: the `ComponentDigest` brand, `componentDigest()` and `componentAddress()`, the required `digest` and `digestBasis` on `ComponentDescriptor`, and the `ScopedLayers` layering with `list({ kind, scope })` and the derived `layer`. Updates `dsh-components-subagents` (the `agent-provider` canonical value `[provider]`, basis `registration`) and `dsh-command-components` (the invoking agent becomes the viewing scope; its rendered line still names no digest or layer, because no runnable example composes `/components` and a rendering change owes a keyless snapshot), [`docs/subsystems/components.md`](../../../../docs/subsystems/components.md), and the three package READMEs.
103	2. The composition-time adapters and their canonical values: `dsh-components-tools`, `dsh-components-prompt`, and `dsh-components-presets` at `packages/components/`, each following its seam's existing change event.
104	3. `dsh-components-manifest`: the `composition/manifest` declaration, the `agent/pre-step` writer with `compositionSha256` deduplication, the regenerated `known-event-types.ts` and persistence catalog, and the `composition-manifest` fixture.
105	4. Skill generations: `skillDigest()` in `dsh-skill`, the `digest` field on the `skill` tool's canonical value and on `SkillInvocationSource`, `dsh-components-skills`, and the mutation fixture.
106	5. Dynamic packages: `cordis/dynamic-changed` on `dsh-cordis-host-runner`, `dsh-components-packages` over `ctx.loader.entries()` and the dynamic runner, and the quarantine fixture.
107	6. Quarantine consumers: the `composition` group and `skillsUsed` on `SessionFacts`, the scorekeeper invariant relation, and `includeQuarantined` with the `quarantined` count in `dsh-trajectories`.
108	7. `dsh-archive`: the domain spec, the `variants` and `generations` tables, the four statuses and their transitions, the two-ended lineage edges, and the manifest-versus-ledger invariant.
109	
110	## Risks
111	
112	A `registration`-basis digest cannot detect a change in what a provider-evaluated prompt section produced, so two runs whose dynamic sections differed share an address. `request/header` carries those bytes and a comparison that needs them must read it; a leaderboard keyed on the manifest alone will pool the two.
113	
114	A `plugin` digest keys on package name and version, and every workspace package here is `0.0.1`, so a source edit does not move it. `HarnessVariant`'s base commit plus patch-set hash is what addresses harness source, and a comparison that keys on plugin digests alone will pool generations of the same package.
115	
116	The manifest names components, not their transitive effects. An MCP server whose remote tool descriptions change without a re-registration, or a skill whose body references a file that changed, keeps its digest; only what the canonical value covers is addressed.
117	
118	Required-on-read means a build that does not know `composition/manifest` refuses a log containing it. That is the intended trade — the alternative is a build silently treating a quarantined session as clean — and it is affordable only under the pre-release stance in the root [AGENTS.md](../../../../AGENTS.md).
119	
120	A composition that churns its visible tool set every step writes one manifest per step. Deduplication by `compositionSha256` keeps a stable composition to exactly one event, and a churning one is paying for a real change in what the model can call, but a scoped restriction toggled per step would inflate a log with events no consumer distinguishes.

195	  private view(scope: ScopeKey | undefined): Map<string, StoredComponent> {

# AGENTS.md — Harness Packages

These package-specific rules supplement the repo-wide [conventions](../AGENTS.md#conventions).

- **Plugin exports:** service packages default-export their service class; function plugins named-export `name` / `inject` / `Config` / `apply` and have no default export. Mixing the forms makes the Loader discard the function plugin's namespace ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **Optional services use `ctx.get(name)`.** Reserve `ctx.<name>` for declared injections; the property proxy is topology-sensitive, while strict `ctx.get` reads the global service store ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **Product-visible plugins require a non-unit REAL-composition test.** Hand-built `ctx.plugin(...)` suites are insufficient. Boot test-only `cordis.yml` through the Loader and app/process; mock only external services or nondeterministic inputs and assert model-visible, durable, or user-visible output. Keep opt-ins out of shipped defaults. [Policy](../docs/testing.md).
- **Initiator-owned private chains derive, then capture.** Under `ctx.agents.withInitiator()`, recover the Agent at each orchestration entry, derive `agent.session`, and let operation-local helpers close over it. Keep `Agent` and `Session` explicit at lifecycle, session-log, service, authority, worker/process, persistence, and wire interfaces; do not widen a leaf helper from `Session` to `Context` merely to hide a parameter ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-15-agent-initiator-scope.md)).
- **Represent one asynchronous operation with one lifecycle controller or transaction.** Separate readiness, cancellation, disposal, reservation, or sentinel state requires an independent owner or settlement point; otherwise fold it while preserving rollback, callback containment, and quiescence.

1	/**
2	 * Mirrors subagent providers into the component registry as `agent-provider`
3	 * components, following the subagent seam's own provider events.
4	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-components-subagents
5	 */
6	
7	import type { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
8	import { ComponentId, componentDigest } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-components'
9	import type {
10	  ComponentDescriptor,
11	  ComponentDigest,
12	  ComponentId as ComponentIdType,
13	} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-components/types'
14	// Type-only: resolves ctx.subagents and the subagent lifecycle events.
15	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent'
16	
17	export const name = 'components-subagents'
18	export const inject = ['components', 'subagents']
19	
20	/** Kind-specific detail of an `agent-provider` component. */
21	export interface AgentProviderComponentDetail {
22	  /** Provider name as registered with `ctx.subagents`. */
23	  readonly provider: string
24	}
25	
26	declare module '@deepseek-ai/dsh-components/types' {
27	  interface ComponentKindMap {
28	    /**
29	     * One subagent provider registered with `ctx.subagents`. The callable
30	     * route is the `subagent` tool instance configured for the provider; the
31	     * subagent seam does not expose that binding, so the component carries
32	     * no `invoke` pointer.
33	     */
34	    'agent-provider': AgentProviderComponentDetail
35	  }
36	}
37	
38	const OWNER = '@deepseek-ai/dsh-components-subagents'
39	
40	/**
41	 * Component id of one subagent provider.
42	 * @param provider - provider name as registered with `ctx.subagents`.
43	 * @returns the stable id `agent-provider:<provider>`.
44	 */
45	export function agentProviderComponentId(provider: string): ComponentIdType {
46	  return ComponentId(`agent-provider:${provider}`)
47	}
48	
49	/**
50	 * Content address of one `agent-provider` component. The canonical value is
51	 * `[provider]`, so the digest addresses the registration and not the agent
52	 * the provider starts: the subagent seam exposes a provider name and its
53	 * lifecycle edges, never the composition behind them, which is why this kind's
54	 * `digestBasis` is `registration`.
55	 * @param provider - provider name as registered with `ctx.subagents`.
56	 * @returns the digest over this kind and that canonical value.
57	 */
58	export function agentProviderDigest(provider: string): ComponentDigest {
59	  return componentDigest('agent-provider', [provider])
60	}
61	
62	/** Describe one provider as a component. */
63	function describeProvider(provider: string): ComponentDescriptor {
64	  return {
65	    id: agentProviderComponentId(provider),
66	    kind: 'agent-provider',
67	    digest: agentProviderDigest(provider),
68	    digestBasis: 'registration',
69	    name: provider,
70	    description: `Subagent provider "${provider}", reached through the subagent tool instance configured for it.`,
71	    owner: OWNER,
72	    provenance: 'curated',
73	    detail: { provider },
74	  }
75	}
76	
77	/**
78	 * Register every current provider and follow later additions and removals.
79	 * @param ctx - Cordis context carrying the component registry and the subagent seam.
80	 */
81	export function apply(ctx: Context): void {
82	  const disposers = new Map<string, () => void>()
83	  const add = (provider: string): void => {
84	    if (disposers.has(provider)) return
85	    disposers.set(provider, ctx.components.register(describeProvider(provider)))
86	  }
87	  const remove = (provider: string): void => {
88	    const dispose = disposers.get(provider)
89	    if (dispose === undefined) return
90	    disposers.delete(provider)
91	    dispose()
92	  }
93	  for (const provider of ctx.subagents.list()) add(provider)
94	  ctx.on('subagent/provider-added', (provider) => { add(provider.name) })
95	  ctx.on('subagent/provider-removed', (provider) => { remove(provider) })
96	  ctx.effect(() => () => {
97	    for (const dispose of disposers.values()) dispose()
98	    disposers.clear()
99	  }, 'components-subagents teardown')
100	}

1	# @deepseek-ai/dsh-components-subagents
2	
3	English | [中文](README.zh.md)
4	
5	Mirrors every subagent provider registered with `ctx.subagents` into the component registry as an `agent-provider` component, following the seam's own `subagent/provider-added` and `subagent/provider-removed` events so the inventory tracks the live registry.
6	
7	## Config
8	
9	```yaml
10	- id: subagents
11	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent'
12	- id: components
13	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-components'
14	- id: components-subagents
15	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-components-subagents'
16	```
17	
18	The adapter takes no configuration and requires both services.
19	
20	## Contract
21	
22	At mount the adapter registers one component per name in `ctx.subagents.list()`; afterwards it registers on `subagent/provider-added` and disposes on `subagent/provider-removed`, ignoring a duplicate addition or an unknown removal. Each component has id `agent-provider:<provider>`, kind `agent-provider`, `provenance: 'curated'`, no `invoke` pointer, and `detail: { provider }`. Disposing the adapter fiber removes every component it registered. `agentProviderComponentId(provider)` builds the id for consumers.
23	
24	This adapter owns the `agent-provider` canonical value beside its `ComponentKindMap` declaration: `[provider]`, addressed by `agentProviderDigest(provider)` with `digestBasis: 'registration'`. The digest covers the registration and not the agent a provider starts, because the subagent seam exposes a provider name and its lifecycle edges, never the composition behind them.
25	
26	## Model Experience
27	
28	None, as the adapter registers component metadata only; the subagent tool owns every model-visible effect of the mirrored providers.
29	
30	#### KV Cache effect
31	
32	None; the adapter neither adds to nor changes any model request.
33	
34	## Known Limitations and Deferred Work
35	
36	- **No callable route** — the `subagent` tool is mounted per provider under a configurable `toolName` and takes no `provider` argument, and the subagent seam does not expose which tool instance is bound to a provider; the component carries no `invoke` pointer until the tools adapter mirrors tool-subagent instances with their provider binding.
37	- **Names only** — the component detail carries the provider name; provider capabilities (`outputSchema`, `depthLimit`, `toolFilter`, `persona`) are not mirrored until a consumer needs them. The digest inherits that limit: two providers of the same name registered by different plugins address identically, and a provider whose capabilities change without a re-registration keeps its digest.
38	- **Global registrations only** — the adapter mounts on a host context, so its components land in the global layer; a per-agent subagent registry would need the adapter mounted through that agent's scope.
39	- **Curated provenance for every provider** — providers are composed plugins today; a synthesized provider registered at runtime would need its producer to declare its own provenance and lineage.
40

11	class StubSubagentRuntime extends Service {
12	  providers: string[] = ['spawn-in-process', 'codex']
13	
14	  constructor(ctx: Context) {
15	    super(ctx, 'subagents')
16	  }
17	
18	  list(): string[] {
19	    return [...this.providers]
20	  }
21	}
22	
23	async function harness() {
24	  const ctx = new Context()
25	  await ctx.plugin(ComponentRegistry)
26	  await ctx.plugin(StubSubagentRuntime)

28	  return { ctx, fiber }
29	}

31	describe('@deepseek-ai/dsh-components-subagents', () => {
32	  it('mirrors every provider present at mount without a callable route', async () => {
33	    const { ctx } = await harness()
34	    expect(adapter.name).toBe('components-subagents')
35	    expect(adapter.inject).toEqual(['components', 'subagents'])
36	    expect(ctx.components.list({ kind: 'agent-provider' }).map(component => component.id)).toEqual([
37	      'agent-provider:spawn-in-process',
38	      'agent-provider:codex',
39	    ])
40	    const codex = ctx.components.get(agentProviderComponentId('codex'))
41	    expect(codex).toMatchObject({
42	      kind: 'agent-provider',
43	      name: 'codex',
44	      provenance: 'curated',
45	      owner: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-components-subagents',
46	      layer: 'global',
47	      detail: { provider: 'codex' },
48	    })
49	    // The subagent tool is mounted per provider under a configurable name and takes no provider argument.
50	    expect(codex?.invoke).toBeUndefined()
51	  })
52	
53	  it('addresses a provider by the canonical value this adapter owns', async () => {
54	    const { ctx } = await harness()
55	    const codex = ctx.components.get(agentProviderComponentId('codex'))
56	    expect(codex?.digest).toBe(componentDigest('agent-provider', ['codex']))
57	    expect(codex?.digest).toBe(agentProviderDigest('codex'))
58	    expect(codex?.digestBasis).toBe('registration')
59	    expect(agentProviderDigest('spawn-in-process')).not.toBe(agentProviderDigest('codex'))
60	  })
61	
62	  it('follows provider additions and removals through the seam events', async () => {
63	    const { ctx } = await harness()
64	    ctx.emit('subagent/provider-added', { name: 'acp' } as never)
65	    expect(ctx.components.get(agentProviderComponentId('acp'))).toBeDefined()
66	    ctx.emit('subagent/provider-added', { name: 'acp' } as never)
67	    expect(ctx.components.list({ kind: 'agent-provider' })).toHaveLength(3)
68	    ctx.emit('subagent/provider-removed', 'codex')
69	    expect(ctx.components.get(agentProviderComponentId('codex'))).toBeUndefined()
70	    ctx.emit('subagent/provider-removed', 'never-registered')
71	    expect(ctx.components.list({ kind: 'agent-provider' }).map(component => component.name)).toEqual(['spawn-in-process', 'acp'])
72	  })
73	
74	  it('removes every mirrored component when the adapter fiber is disposed', async () => {
75	    const { ctx, fiber } = await harness()
76	    expect(ctx.components.list({ kind: 'agent-provider' })).toHaveLength(2)
77	    await fiber.dispose()
78	    expect(ctx.components.list({ kind: 'agent-provider' })).toHaveLength(0)
79	  })

82	    const ctx = new Context()

84	    await ctx.plugin(InvariantRegistry, { enabled: true })

145	  interface Events {
146	    /**
147	     * Allow, deny, or ask before dispatch. `next()` delegates to allow; missing
148	     * approval support turns `ask` into denial. Async gates must observe
149	     * `exec.signal`; the registry rechecks cancellation after they settle but
150	     * never abandons their promise.
151	     * Scope-filtered dispatch (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-scope`): agent-scoped listeners receive only that agent's calls.
152	     * @param exec - the pending call (name, parsed arguments, caller agent).
153	     * @mode waterfall
154	     */
155	    'tools/pre-execute'(this: Scoped<ToolRuntime>, exec: ToolExecution, next: () => Promise<PreToolDecision>): Promise<PreToolDecision>
156	    /**
157	     * Around-dispatch waterfall for timeout, retry, or metrics. `next()` returns
158	     * a normalized result; wrappers may change only `exec.signal`, while call
159	     * identity remains immutable. The registry re-fuses the original caller
160	     * signal before the body, so replacement cannot detach caller cancellation;
161	     * wrappers must still restore their signal and reach quiescence.
162	     * Scope-filtered dispatch (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-scope`): agent-scoped listeners receive only that agent's calls.
163	     * @param exec - the allowed call about to dispatch (name, parsed arguments, caller agent, signal).
164	     * @mode waterfall
165	     */
166	    'tools/execute'(this: Scoped<ToolRuntime>, exec: ToolDispatchExecution, next: () => Promise<ToolExecutionResult>): Promise<ToolExecutionResult>
167	    /**
168	     * Accept, replace, enrich, or block a normalized dispatch result. `next()`
169	     * accepts it unchanged; thrown tools still reach this waterfall as errors. Async
170	     * listeners must observe `exec.signal`; after they settle, caller
171	     * cancellation replaces only a successful accepted outcome with the code
172	     * selected by whether the tool body was invoked.
173	     * Scope-filtered dispatch (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-scope`): agent-scoped listeners receive only that agent's calls.
174	     * @param exec - the call that just ran (name, parsed arguments, caller agent).
175	     * @param result - the dispatch outcome a listener may accept, replace, or block.
176	     * @mode waterfall
177	     */
178	    'tools/post-execute'(this: Scoped<ToolRuntime>, exec: ToolExecution, result: Readonly<ToolExecutionResult>, next: () => Promise<PostToolDecision>): Promise<PostToolDecision>
179	    /**
180	     * Allow a listener to replace content in the DURABLE LOG COPY of one
181	     * `run_code` sub-dispatch outcome before the bridge appends its
182	     * `tool/code-dispatch` event. `next()` keeps the
183	     * content unchanged; a listener may return replacement blocks (e.g. the
184	     * spill policy's preview + locator for an oversized text result). Only the
185	     * logged copy is affected — the program already received the complete
186	     * value, and the model sees neither. A throwing listener is contained:
187	     * the bridge falls back to logging the original settled content.
188	     * Scope-filtered dispatch (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-scope`): agent-scoped listeners receive only that agent's dispatches.
189	     * @param dispatch - the parent execution, sub-call identity, and the settled content to log.
190	     * @mode waterfall
191	     */
192	    'tools/code-dispatch-log'(this: Scoped<ToolRuntime>, dispatch: CodeDispatchLog, next: () => Promise<ContentBlock[]>): Promise<ContentBlock[]>
193	    /**
194	     * Observe the frozen, lossless-JSON final outcome. Listener failures are contained.
195	     * Scope-filtered dispatch (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-scope`): keyed by `exec.agent`.
196	     * @param exec - the execution object that traversed the pipeline.
197	     * @param result - a deep-frozen snapshot of the final returned result.
198	     * @mode emit
199	     */
200	    'tools/result'(this: Scoped<ToolRuntime>, exec: Readonly<ToolExecution>, result: Readonly<ToolExecutionResult>): undefined
201	    /**
202	     * A tool was registered or unregistered, or a scoped restriction changed
203	     * (the available tool set changed — possibly for one scope only). An
204	     * UNFILTERED registry-subject notification, deliberately not scope-filtered
205	     * dispatch: a global change concerns every agent's next assembly, so a
206	     * scoped listener subscribing here sees every change, not just its own
207	     * scope's.
208	     * @mode emit
209	     */
210	    'tools/change'(): void
211	  }
212	}

224	/** A registered tool: its schema plus the execution function. */
225	export interface ToolDefinition extends ToolSchema {
226	  /** Mandatory canonical output declaration. */
227	  readonly output: ToolOutputDefinition
228	  /**
229	   * Run one accepted call and return only its canonical lossless-JSON value.
230	   * Async work must observe or forward `exec.signal` and settle only after its
231	   * owned work reaches quiescence. The registry preserves caller cancellation
232	   * through around-dispatch signal replacement and does not abandon this
233	   * promise, but it cannot hard-kill same-process code.
234	   * @param args - losslessly snapshotted, frozen model arguments.
235	   * @param exec - execution identity, cancellation signal, and context deferral.
236	   * @returns the canonical value declared by `output.schema`.
237	   */
238	  execute(args: unknown, exec: ToolRunContext): Promise<unknown>
239	  /**
240	   * Synchronous last-mile transform for model-facing content. The registry
241	   * snapshots this callback when execution starts and invokes it exactly once
242	   * for every normalized outcome, including pipeline failures that bypass
243	   * `tools/post-execute`, immediately before lossless materialization.
244	   * Returning `undefined` preserves the content; every other result field
245	   * remains registry-owned. The callback must be total and must not throw.
246	   * @param exec - immutable execution identity and arguments.
247	   * @param result - complete normalized outcome before materialization.
248	   * @returns replacement content, or `undefined` to preserve it.
249	   */
250	  finalizeContent?(exec: Readonly<ToolExecution>, result: Readonly<ToolExecutionResult>): ContentBlock[] | undefined
251	  /**
252	   * Cooperative tool-call timeout budget in milliseconds. Omit for no deadline.
253	   * Enforced by `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-call-timeout-policy` (a `tools/execute` wrapper); it
254	   * is NEVER sent to the model — `schemas()` whitelists only name/description/
255	   * parameters. Declaring it asserts this tool forwards `exec.signal` to a
256	   * cooperative implementation that can reach quiescence when the signal aborts.
257	   */
258	  timeoutMs?: number
259	  /**
260	   * Privileged reach this tool holds beyond the workspace, empty when it holds
261	   * none. NEVER model-visible — `schemas()` whitelists only name/description/
262	   * parameters — and never enforced here: the declaration is what a composition
263	   * audit and a session's `tools.guard()` read to refuse a tool whose authority
264	   * the calling session's role forbids.
265	   */
266	  authority?: readonly ToolAuthority[]
267	  /**
268	   * Pure synchronous classifier for overlap with sibling tool calls. Only
269	   * `true` opts in; omission, exceptions, non-`true` returns, and invalid
270	   * `defineTool` arguments are exclusive. This metadata is never model-visible.
271	   *
272	   * Opted-in executions must not mutate parent-owned state. Shared state must
273	   * tolerate concurrent dispatch; recorder races are permitted only when they
274	   * commute or fail closed. See the
275	   * [parallel-tool-call Agent Note](../../../../.agents/notes/implemented/feature/2026-07-10-parallel-tool-call-execution.md)
276	   * for the full contract.
277	   * @param args - parsed arguments; `defineTool` validates before calling.
278	   * @returns Whether this call may join a parallel group.
279	   */
280	  isConcurrencySafe?(args: unknown): boolean
281	  /**
282	   * Optional: how to present the PENDING state of one call in a UI, derived from
283	   * the call's `args` (parsed arguments, `unknown` — the tool validates/narrows
284	   * its own input). Returns a {@link ToolCallView} (a `card`-tagged render intent),
285	   * or `undefined` (or omit the method) to fall back to a generic presentation
286	   * (title = tool name, raw args as input). Pure and side-effect-free: a UI may
287	   * call it during live streaming AND a session-log replay, so it must depend
288	   * only on `args`.
289	   */
290	  presentCall?(args: unknown): ToolCallView | undefined
291	  /**
292	   * Optional: how to present the COMPLETED state, given the same `args` and the
293	   * durable result projection (`content`, failure state, and optional `meta`). Returns a
294	   * {@link ToolResultView}, or `undefined` (or omit the method) to keep the
295	   * pending title and render the raw result content. Pure and side-effect-free
296	   * for the same replay reason.
297	   */
298	  presentResult?(args: unknown, result: ToolResult): ToolResultView | undefined
299	}

499	/**
500	 * Thrown (internally) when the model requests a tool that isn't registered.
501	 * Extends {@link HarnessError} (`code: 'UNKNOWN_TOOL'`) so an unknown-tool
502	 * failure is as routable as a tool-thrown one — retry/sandbox/replay code can
503	 * distinguish it from a tool body's own error.
504	 */
505	export class ToolNotFoundError extends HarnessError {
506	  /**
507	   * @param toolName - the name the caller asked for.
508	   * @param reachableFrom - how the model reaches this tool instead, when the
509	   *   name IS visible and only the presentation denies calling it directly.
510	   *   Omitted for a name that is registered nowhere.
511	   */
512	  constructor(toolName: string, reachableFrom?: string) {
513	    super(

=== README ===
# dsh-scope

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Scoped registration primitive. `createScope(ctx, key)` creates a tagged Cordis context whose backing fiber owns every registration made through it. `scopeOf(ctx)` reads the tag, and `scopeTarget(base, key)` routes scoped events to listeners with the same key while leaving unscoped listeners global. Keys form an optional parent chain (`bindScopeParent`): registration views inherit DOWN it — a child scope sees its ancestors' layers, nearest shadowing farthest — and event admission extends UP it — a listener tagged with an ancestor receives a descendant key's events, never the reverse. The agent loop creates one scope per live agent and an agent preset's standing mount is a parent scope over its agents, but the mechanism is key-agnostic so lower-level packages can use it without depending on either.

## Public API

- `createScope(ctx: Context, key: ScopeKey, options?): Scope` Mint a scope under `ctx`'s fiber. Usable synchronously (effect collection is uid-gated; service resolution falls through to the minting plugin's dependency surface). The typed, same-process key is trusted; an inactive minting context still fails through Cordis (`INACTIVE_EFFECT`). `options.parent` binds the enclosing scope via `bindScopeParent` before the scope is usable; the binding stays internal.
- `bindScopeParent(key, parent): ScopeParentBinding` / `scopeParentOf(key)` / `scopeChainOf(key)` The parent relation behind both chain directions. Binding is once: a key that already has a parent throws, and only the returned binding's `rebind(parent)` may re-link it — the blank-session recompose operation, valid only while nothing produced under the old parent is retained (the holder's contract — this relation cannot see what a session logged). Both the bind and every rebind reject a link closing a cycle. `scopeChainOf` returns `[key, parent, …]` nearest-first.
- `Scope.ctx` The tagged context: registrations through it are scope-visible AND scope-lifetime. Derived contexts (an `extend`, a fiber mounted under it) inherit the tag; nested scopes shadow (nearest tag wins).
- `Scope.rawDispose` The EXACT Cordis disposer for the backing fiber — a composite (generator) effect yields THIS function to nest the scope's teardown at that yield position (Cordis dedupes nested effects by function identity; yielding a wrapper leaves the scope disposing as a concurrent sibling).
- `Scope.dispose(): Promise<void>` Idempotent, shared quiescence boundary for every registration made through the scope. Racing/repeat calls await the same teardown, including when `rawDispose` invoked the underlying single-shot Cordis disposer first.
- `scopeOf(ctx: Context): ScopeKey | undefined` The tag a context (or any context derived from it) carries; `undefined` = context-global.
- `scopeTarget(base: T, key: ScopeKey | undefined): Scoped<T>` Build the opaque dispatch `thisArg` for a scope-filtered event. It composes `base`'s existing `Context.filter` with the scope predicate (untagged listener ⇒ admitted; tagged ⇒ admitted iff its tag is the key or an ancestor of it; `key === undefined` ⇒ untagged only). The carrier contains routing state only; the real subject is carried by the event arguments. `{ global: true }` listeners bypass filtering (Cordis semantics).
- `Scoped<T>` The compile-time opaque carrier brand: scope-filtered events demand it as their `this` type, so dispatching with a bare subject is a compile error. The type parameter records the subject type but does not expose its properties.
- `isScopeCarrier(value)` / `carrierKeyOf(value)` Runtime carrier marks, used by the dev invariants to assert every scope-filtered dispatch carries a carrier keyed to the subject its arguments name.
- `ScopeLayer` Aggregate contract for one registry's complete global or exact-scope contribution; `isEmpty()` controls scoped-layer reclamation.
- `ScopedLayers<L>` Own one eager global layer and lazy exact-scope layers. `peek()` never creates and stays chain-blind (a scope's OWN contributions — restrictions, guards — must not silently pick up an ancestor's), `chainLayers()` returns existing overlays farthest-ancestor-first, `merge()` materializes insertion-ordered named shadows along the chain, and `effect()` derives visibility and ownership from the same context while returning the exact Cordis disposer.
- `NamedEntries<V>` Insertion-ordered named storage with caller-owned duplicate diagnostics, lookup, and live iteration within one nonempty table generation; draining the table detaches existing iterators from later insertions, and `insert()` returns an idempotent exact-entry undo.
- `AnonymousEntries<V>` Insertion-ordered anonymous storage whose unique internal keys keep equal values as independent registrations; it uses the same drained-generation iterator boundary, and `append()` returns an idempotent exact-entry undo.

The optional `@deepseek-ai/dsh-scope/invariant` companion owns that runtime assertion. It uses the generated `scoped-events.generated.ts` resolver map to require a carrier for every declared scoped event and, when the payload exposes its routing subject, require identity with the carrier key. The Program-backed generator derives the map from event declarations and real `scopeTarget(base, key)` calls.

## Design contract

The registration context determines both visibility and ownership, preventing a registration from being visible in one scope but disposed with another. Scopes route trusted same-process plugins; they are not sandboxes or authority boundaries. See the [agent-scope Agent Note](../../../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-08-agent-scope-contexts.md#security-and-authority-are-non-goals) for rationale and security non-goals.

Scope-aware services define a concrete `ScopeLayer` that aggregates their heterogeneous tables and domain helpers. `ScopedLayers.effect()` accepts one synchronous action returning one synchronous undo, installs that undo before optional notification, and reclaims an exact-scope layer only when the complete aggregate is empty. `notify` defaults to `true`; the supplied callback owns whether observer failures throw or are contained. `EntryValues` remains internal, the storage classes are imported from the package root rather than a `/store` subpath, and the shared storage does not define registry-specific filtering or iteration policy. See the [shared scoped-layer storage Agent Note](../../../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-12-scoped-layers-store.md).

Handing out a scoped context hands out the minting plugin's service-resolution API (resolution walks the minting fiber's dependency chain, not the holder's) — mint it from the plugin whose dependencies the scoped registrations need to resolve.

## Known Limitations and Deferred Work

- **Only scope-aware APIs isolate state** — registries must file by `scopeOf()` and events must dispatch through `scopeTarget()`; an arbitrary Cordis service remains context-global merely because it is called through a scoped context.
- **A context carries one nearest scope key** — the hierarchy lives in the key-level parent relation, not in context tags; nested scope CONTEXTS still shadow to a single tag, and multi-membership policy sets remain unsupported.
- **Service reachability comes from the scope minter** — handing out `Scope.ctx` also hands out the minting plugin's injected services, so a broader minter cannot later be narrowed by the holder.

173	 * subtree in one runtime would be blamed for a service published in another.
174	 * @param fiber - the fiber to locate.
175	 * @param root - the subtree root to test membership against.
176	 * @returns true when `fiber` belongs to `root`'s subtree.
177	 */
178	function withinFiber(fiber: Fiber, root: Fiber): boolean {
179	  let current = fiber
180	  while (true) {
181	    if (current === root) return true
182	    const parent = current.parent.fiber
183	    if (parent === current) return false
184	    current = parent
185	  }
186	}
187	
188	/**
189	 * Service names the mounted subtree published into the root realm.
190	 *
191	 * A provider without an `isolate` realm stores its implementation under the
192	 * root's symbol for that name, which is exactly the comparison below; a
193	 * provider inside an `isolate` realm stores under a realm-private symbol and
194	 * is correctly absent here.
195	 * @param ctx - any context of the runtime whose service store is inspected.
196	 * @param mount - the mounted subtree's fiber.
197	 * @returns the leaked service names in lexical order.
198	 */
199	export function leakedServices(ctx: Context, mount: Fiber): string[] {
200	  const store = ctx.reflect.store
201	  const rootIsolate = ctx.root[Context.isolate]
202	  const leaked: string[] = []
203	  for (const key of Object.getOwnPropertySymbols(store)) {
204	    const impl = store[key]
205	    /* v8 ignore next -- cordis deletes a store slot on disposal rather than
206	       clearing it, so an own symbol always resolves; the guard exists only
207	       because the store's index signature is optional. */
208	    if (impl === undefined) continue
209	    if (!withinFiber(impl.fiber, mount)) continue
210	    if (rootIsolate[impl.name] === key) leaked.push(impl.name)
211	  }
212	  return leaked.sort((left, right) => left.localeCompare(right))
213	}
214	
215	/** A live standing mount located through one agent already joined to it. */
216	export type JoinedPresetMount = PresetMount & {
217	  /** The standing key, definite because it is what the lookup matched on. */
218	  readonly key: ScopeKey
219	}
220	
221	/**
222	 * The standing composition one agent is joined to.
223	 *
224	 * The agent's own key is parented to its preset's standing key, so the mount
225	 * is found by matching that parent rather than by walking up from the agent —
226	 * the mount is not under the agent's fiber. An agent that joined no preset —
227	 * a deployment composing no roster, or a child agent before its join — has no
228	 * parent link and resolves to undefined.
229	 * @param agentCtx - the agent's scope context.
230	 * @returns the mount the agent joined, or undefined when it joined none.
231	 */
232	export function standingMountFor(agentCtx: Context): JoinedPresetMount | undefined {
233	  const agentKey = scopeOf(agentCtx)
234	  if (agentKey === undefined) return undefined
235	  const standingKey = scopeParentOf(agentKey)
236	  if (standingKey === undefined) return undefined
237	  return livePresetMounts().find(
238	    (candidate): candidate is JoinedPresetMount => candidate.key === standingKey,
239	  )
240	}
241	
242	/**
243	 * One agent's instance of a service its preset mounted.
244	 *
245	 * A preset publishes a service behind an `isolate` realm so two sessions
246	 * cannot collide, and an entry-local realm is invisible to everything outside
247	 * the group — including the agent's own scope context and the host. That is
248	 * right for the rows inside the group and wrong for one caller: a request that
249	 * is ABOUT a session but arrives from outside it, which is every browser RPC
250	 * the api-proxy serves.
251	 *
252	 * Ownership is the same relation {@link leakedServices} reads, inverted: there
253	 * it names implementations a subtree published into the ROOT realm, here it
254	 * names the one this subtree published anywhere. Fiber membership is object
255	 * identity for the reason stated on {@link withinFiber}.
256	 *
257	 * This is READ addressing for a caller that already holds the agent. It is not
258	 * a general host handle on a session's internals: a host row that `inject`s a
259	 * service cannot use it, because injection resolves before any session exists
260	 * and has no agent to key by — such a service belongs on the host plane.
261	 * @param ctx - any context of the runtime whose service store is inspected.
262	 * @param agent - the agent whose mounted composition to look inside.
263	 * @param name - the service name as the preset's rows resolve it.
264	 * @returns the agent's instance, or undefined when its preset mounts none.
265	 */
266	export function serviceForAgent<K extends string & keyof Context>(
267	  ctx: Context,
268	  agent: { ctx: Context },
269	  name: K,
270	): Context[K] | undefined {
271	  const mount = standingMountFor(agent.ctx)
272	  if (mount === undefined) return undefined
273	  const store = ctx.reflect.store
274	  for (const key of Object.getOwnPropertySymbols(store)) {
275	    const impl = store[key]
276	    /* v8 ignore next -- cordis deletes a store slot on disposal rather than clearing it */
277	    if (impl === undefined) continue
278	    if (impl.name !== name) continue
279	    if (withinFiber(impl.fiber, mount.fiber)) return impl.value as Context[K]
280	  }
281	  return undefined
282	}
283	
284	/**
285	 * Rows that did not reach a usable state, each rendered as one diagnostic line.
286	 *
287	 * A row whose module failed to import or whose plugin threw already rejects the
288	 * mount through the loader; what remains observable here is a row still waiting
289	 * for a service the composition never supplies.
290	 * @param tree - the mounted subtree.
291	 * @returns one line per unusable row, empty when every enabled row is usable.
292	 */
293	export function inactiveRows(tree: EntryTree): string[] {
294	  const lines: string[] = []
295	  for (const entry of tree.entries()) {
296	    if (entry.disabled) continue
297	    const fiber = entry.fiber
298	    /* v8 ignore next 4 -- the loader rejects an entry whose module or plugin failed,
299	       so a settled tree never holds an enabled fiber-less entry; the branch exists
300	       only because `Entry.fiber` is declared optional. */
301	    if (fiber === undefined) {
302	      lines.push(`${entry.options.id} (${entry.options.name}): never started`)
303	      continue
304	    }
305	    const missing = Object.keys(fiber.inject).filter(name => fiber.ctx.get(name) === undefined)
306	    if (missing.length > 0) {
307	      lines.push(`${entry.options.id} (${entry.options.name}): waiting for ${missing.join(', ')}`)
308	    }
309	  }
310	  return lines
311	}
312	
313	/**
314	 * How the composition contradicts the role the preset declared, or undefined
315	 * when it does not.
316	 *
317	 * Read from the scope the preset mounted into, so it covers what a session
318	 * composed from this preset actually sees: the preset's own rows and every
319	 * inherited global row alike. The tool registry is optional because a
320	 * deployment may compose none; without one nothing is composed to audit.
321	 * @param ctx - the standing scope context the subtree was mounted under.
322	 * @param preset - the preset whose declared role is being audited.
323	 * @returns the refusal to throw, or undefined when the composition holds.
324	 */
325	export function roleAudit(ctx: Context, preset: AgentPreset): PresetRoleError | undefined {
326	  const role: ReadBarrierRole = preset.role ?? 'unrestricted'
327	  const tools = ctx.get('tools')
328	  if (tools === undefined) return undefined
329	  const scope = scopeOf(ctx)
330	  for (const schema of tools.schemas(scope)) {
331	    const denied = deniedAuthority(role, tools.get(schema.name, scope)?.authority)
332	    if (denied === undefined) continue
333	    return new PresetRoleError(preset.id, role, schema.name, denied)
334	  }
335	  return undefined
336	}
337	
338	/**
339	 * The reportable text of a mount failure.
340	 *
341	 * The loader reports several failed rows as one `AggregateError`, whose own
342	 * message names none of them; without flattening, a composition that fails on
343	 * two rows says only "loader entries failed to apply" and the operator has
344	 * nothing to act on.
345	 * @param error - the value the mount rejected with.
346	 * @returns a single-line-per-cause description.
347	 */
348	function mountDetail(error: unknown): string {
349	  /* v8 ignore next -- every path into the mount's catch throws an Error: the loader
350	     wraps a row's thrown value before it propagates, and this module's own
351	     rejections are Errors. The fallback keeps a hostile value readable. */
352	  if (!(error instanceof Error)) return String(error)
353	  if (!(error instanceof AggregateError)) return error.message
354	  return [error.message, ...error.errors.map(cause => `- ${mountDetail(cause)}`)].join('\n')
355	}
356	
357	/**
358	 * Mount `preset` under `agentCtx` and return only once every row is usable.
359	 *
360	 * The subtree is owned by `agentCtx`'s fiber, so it unwinds with the agent and
361	 * the caller receives no disposer. A rejection leaves nothing mounted.
362	 * @param agentCtx - the agent's scope context, from the agent factory's `setup`.
363	 * @param preset - the resolved preset to compose the agent from.
364	 * @throws when `agentCtx` carries no scope, a row is unusable, or a row
365	 * published a service into the root realm.
366	 */
367	export async function mountPreset(agentCtx: Context, preset: AgentPreset): Promise<void> {
368	  const scope = scopeOf(agentCtx)
369	  if (scope === undefined) {
370	    throw new Error(
371	      `agent-presets: refusing to mount preset "${preset.id}" into an unscoped context; `
372	      + 'its registrations would apply to every agent in the process',
373	    )
374	  }
375	  const config: Include.Config = { path: pathToFileURL(preset.path).href }
376	  // Captured before the subtree exists: the standing scope context still
377	  // carries the host composition's base, which is inside the installed
378	  // harness and is therefore where a row's package name has to resolve from.
379	  /* v8 ignore next -- the Loader sets `baseUrl` on the root before any scoped context derives from it */
380	  if (agentCtx.baseUrl !== undefined) harnessBase.set(config, agentCtx.baseUrl)
381	  // Before the record this mount is about to add: standing mounts are one per
382	  // preset and live until whole-tree teardown, so pruning here only sweeps
383	  // records of torn-down runtimes (tests; an HMR reload of the roster).
384	  pruneDisposedMounts()
385	  const handle = agentCtx.plugin(PresetTree, config)
386	  try {
387	    await handle.await()
388	    const subtree = mounted.get(config)
389	    /* v8 ignore next -- the subclass constructor runs before `await()` settles for every mounted tree */
390	    if (subtree === undefined) throw new Error('mounted subtree did not publish its entry tree')
391	    const { tree, fiber } = subtree
392	    const unusable = inactiveRows(tree)
393	    if (unusable.length > 0) {
394	      throw new Error(`${String(unusable.length)} row(s) did not activate:\n${unusable.join('\n')}`)
395	    }
396	    const leaked = leakedServices(agentCtx, fiber)
397	    if (leaked.length > 0) {
398	      throw new Error(
399	        `row(s) published process-global service(s) [${leaked.join(', ')}]; `
400	        + 'a preset service must sit behind an `isolate` realm or move to the host composition',
401	      )
402	    }
403	    // After the subtree settles, beside `inactiveRows`: the audit reads the
404	    // registry the rows actually contributed to, not the file they came from.
405	    const refusal = roleAudit(agentCtx, preset)
406	    if (refusal !== undefined) throw refusal
407	    mounts.add({
408	      presetId: preset.id, fiber, key: scopeOf(agentCtx),
409	      ...preset.role === undefined ? {} : { role: preset.role },
410	    })
411	  } catch (error) {
412	    try {
413	      await handle.dispose()
414	    /* v8 ignore next 5 -- teardown of a subtree nothing else references has no
415	       observed failure mode; the guard exists so a teardown error cannot
416	       replace the mount diagnostic the caller needs. */
417	    } catch {
418	      // Swallows only this subtree's teardown failure. The mount error below is
419	      // the actionable one, and the discarded fiber is unreachable either way.
420	    }
421	    // Reported as authored: the authority refusal names the tool and the
422	    // authority to remove, which a "failed to mount" wrapper would bury.
423	    if (error instanceof PresetRoleError) throw error
424	    throw new PresetMountError(preset.id, `${mountDetail(error)} (${preset.path})`, { cause: error })
425	  }
426	}
427

1	/** Agent-preset vocabulary shared by discovery, mounting, and consumers. */
2	
3	import type { ReadBarrierRole } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-read-barrier/types'
4	import type { ToolAuthority } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools/types'
5	
6	/**
7	 * Where a preset's composition came from. A `system` preset ships with the
8	 * deployment; a `user` preset was authored locally, by a person or by an
9	 * agent, and therefore carries the same trust as shell access.
10	 */
11	export type PresetTrust = 'system' | 'user'
12	
13	/**
14	 * Ids a preset directory may use.
15	 *
16	 * The id becomes a path segment, so this is a containment boundary rather than
17	 * a style rule: `..`, a separator, or an absolute-looking name would place the
18	 * composition outside the root the deployment authorised. Discovery shares it:
19	 * a directory whose name no copy could ever claim is not a preset slot.
20	 */
21	export const PRESET_ID = /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$/
22	
23	/** One preset directory that carries a mountable agent composition. */
24	export interface AgentPreset {
25	  /** Stable identifier; the preset directory's name. */
26	  readonly id: string
27	  /** Trust recorded from the root this preset was discovered under. */
28	  readonly trust: PresetTrust
29	  /** Absolute path of the preset's agent composition file. */
30	  readonly path: string
31	  /** Display name from the preset's own metadata; absent falls back to {@link id}. */
32	  readonly name?: string
33	  /** One sentence on what this preset is for, when it published one. */
34	  readonly description?: string
35	  /** Declared position within its group; absent sorts after those that declare one. */
36	  readonly order?: number
37	  /**
38	   * Read-barrier role this preset declares for the sessions it composes, absent
39	   * when it declares none. The one authority claim `preset.yml` carries.
40	   */
41	  readonly role?: ReadBarrierRole
42	  /**
43	   * Why this preset cannot compose a session, absent when it can. A broken
44	   * preset stays on the roster — hiding it would leave its directory blocking
45	   * the id with nothing to see or delete — but every mounting path refuses it
46	   * up front with this reason instead of failing deep inside the loader.
47	   */
48	  readonly broken?: string
49	}
50	
51	/** One directory scanned for preset subdirectories. */
52	export interface PresetRoot {
53	  /** Directory holding one subdirectory per preset; a leading `~` expands. */
54	  path: string
55	  /** Trust recorded on every preset discovered under this root. */
56	  trust: PresetTrust
57	}
58	
59	/** Plugin config: which preset is the default, and where presets live. */
60	export interface Config {
61	  /** Preset id mounted when a caller names none. Missing at mount time fails loud. */
62	  default: string
63	  /** Scanned roots in precedence order; an earlier root wins a duplicate id. */
64	  roots: PresetRoot[]
65	  /**
66	   * Append the harness home's `USER_PRESET_DIR` as a `user` root, after every
67	   * configured root. False mounts a roster over `roots` alone.
68	   */
69	  includeUserRoot: boolean
70	}
71	
72	/**
73	 * No configured root supplies the requested preset.
74	 *
75	 * Separate from a mount failure because the two mean different things to a
76	 * caller: an unknown id is a bad request, while an unusable composition is a
77	 * broken preset the deployment must fix.
78	 */
79	export class UnknownPresetError extends Error {
80	  constructor(
81	    /** The id that was requested. */
82	    readonly presetId: string,
83	    /** Ids the roster does supply, for the caller to offer instead. */
84	    readonly available: readonly string[],
85	  ) {
86	    super(`agent-presets: preset "${presetId}" not found (available: ${available.join(', ') || 'none'})`)
87	  }
88	}
89	
90	/**
91	 * A preset's composition contradicts the role it declared.
92	 *
93	 * Its own class, and reported unwrapped by {@link mountPreset}, because the
94	 * failure is not "this composition is broken" but "this composition may not
95	 * hold what it holds under that role": the exact text names the tool and the
96	 * authority an operator has to remove.
97	 */
98	export class PresetRoleError extends Error {
99	  constructor(
100	    /** The preset whose declaration the composition contradicts. */
101	    readonly presetId: string,
102	    /** The role the preset declared. */
103	    readonly role: ReadBarrierRole,
104	    /** The composed tool the role forbids. */
105	    readonly tool: string,
106	    /** The authority that tool's definition declares. */
107	    readonly authority: ToolAuthority,
108	  ) {
109	    super(`agent-presets: preset "${presetId}" declares role "${role}" but composes "${tool}", which carries the "${authority}" authority`)
110	  }
111	}
112	
113	/** A preset exists but its composition cannot be installed. */
114	export class PresetMountError extends Error {
115	  constructor(
116	    /** The preset whose composition failed. */
117	    readonly presetId: string,
118	    /** Why it failed, without this package's own message prefix. */
119	    readonly reason: string,
120	    options?: ErrorOptions,
121	  ) {
122	    super(`agent-presets: preset "${presetId}" failed to mount: ${reason}`, options)
123	  }
124	}

2	/**
3	 * Test driver: boot the scoreboard composition, run the training-eligible
4	 * environments twice each on the default route, then fold the same cells back
5	 * out of the persisted logs — a scoreboard, the facts of the first certified
6	 * cell, and a JSONL export to `./facts.jsonl` — and print both the fleet's
7	 * in-memory leaderboard and the log-derived one for the e2e's assertions.
8	 */
9	
10	import { boot, resolveConfigPath } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot'
11	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-loader'
12	import { jsonlFileSink } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-trajectories'
13	
14	const configPath = process.argv[2]
15	if (configPath === undefined) throw new Error('scoreboard driver requires a config path')
16	
17	const ctx = await boot('scoreboard-e2e', resolveConfigPath(configPath, undefined))
18	try {
19	  // Loader siblings mount concurrently; the runner creates agents only over the settled application.
20	  await ctx.get('loader')?.await()
21	  const fleet = ctx.get('fleet')
22	  const scorekeeper = ctx.get('scorekeeper')
23	  if (fleet === undefined || scorekeeper === undefined) throw new Error('scoreboard driver requires the fleet and the scorekeeper service')
24	  const report = await fleet.run({
25	    environments: { filter: { heldOut: false } },
26	    models: [],
27	    repetitions: 2,
28	    workspaceRoot: process.cwd(),
29	    group: 'scoreboard-e2e',
30	  })
31	  const certified = report.cells.find(outcome => 'report' in outcome && outcome.report.certified)
32	  if (certified === undefined || !('report' in certified)) throw new Error('scoreboard driver expects one certified cell')
33	  const scoreboard = await scorekeeper.leaderboard({ group: 'scoreboard-e2e' })
34	  const facts = await scorekeeper.facts(certified.report.sessionId)
35	  const exported = await scorekeeper.exportFacts({ sink: jsonlFileSink('./facts.jsonl') })
36	  process.stdout.write(`${JSON.stringify({ type: 'result', leaderboard: report.leaderboard, scoreboard, facts, exported })}\n`)
37	} finally {
38	  await ctx.fiber.dispose()
39	}

# AGENTS.md — Examples

Runnable harness compositions. `examples/` is one workspace member and the module-resolution root for runnable and test Cordis configs; it is not a build target. [package.json](package.json) declares the packages loaded by those configs, while each leaf's private `package.json` remains metadata only.

Extract reusable logic into `packages/`, where per-file coverage and README gates apply. Examples keep only `cordis.yml` wiring, demo artifacts, and e2e/snapshot scenarios; app package bins own boot glue.

## E2E smokes

Each example has both:

- **Keyless:** boot the real `cordis.yml` through the Loader, drive it, and assert output and clean exit. Catches invalid Loader exports that hand-mounted tests miss ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **With-key:** send a live-model prompt and verify external state, not the model's claim. Self-skip without `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`; see [testing.md](../docs/testing.md).

Keyless process smokes use `@deepseek-ai/dsh-loader-smoke` for Loader launch resolution; terminal tests wrap that launch in a pseudo-terminal. Tests supply paths, environment, input, and assertions. Every checked-in test Cordis config lives under its corresponding `examples/<agent>/` leaf. Map a package-owned config to `examples/<agent>/tests/fixtures/<group>/<package>/cordis.yml`, keep its driver and assertions package-local, and declare every package it names in both root `tsconfig.json` references and `examples/package.json`.

Do not inventory example tests here; the `tests/` trees and root scripts are authoritative.

In `cordis.yml`, comment only non-obvious wiring, load-order consequences, replay, security boundaries, and configuration scope. Do not narrate visible entries; use [dsh-prose-standard](../.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for required coverage and editorial judgment.

See [the root AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) for repo-wide conventions and [docs/architecture.md](../docs/architecture.md) for the design.

/** Cached immutable public snapshot of the private append-only log. */
  private eventsSnapshot: readonly SessionEvent[] | undefined

  /**
   * An immutable snapshot of the append-only event log. The snapshot is reused
   * until the next append; a previously returned array does not grow later.
   * Events and their nested data are deep-frozen at acceptance, so neither a
   * cast nor ordinary JavaScript can rewrite durable history.
   */
  get events(): readonly SessionEvent[] {
    this.eventsSnapshot ??= Object.freeze([...this.log])
    return this.eventsSnapshot
  }

  /** The next event's sequence number — always the log length (the `seq = log.length` contiguity contract). */
  get seq(): number {
    return this.log.length

   * the store-owned, module-private publication hooks. The hot path never blocks

   * contained per listener, so they do not change the return value or prevent
   * later listeners from observing the same accepted event.
